description: Lets the agent right-size its own brain for this chat — check the menu of available models and what each can do (vision, image output, premium), switch to a specific model (including a vision or image-output model for image work), upgrade onto a premium model for a hard task (with permission), and tune how hard the model thinks (reasoning effort: minimal → high) per task. Cleanup is automatic: the backend returns the chat to the default model and effort when the run ends, so the agent never needs a closing switch-back step.
skill_summary: How the agent right-sizes its own model AND thinking depth: list_models() to read the menu of available models (with sees-images / makes-images / premium badges + effort levels) so it switches by capability, not by guessing an id; set_model('<id>') to honour a user's model request or take over on a vision/image model; use_premium_model() to upgrade onto the configured premium tier for a hard task; set_effort('minimal'|'low'|'medium'|'high') to rate a task and dial the reasoning effort up for hard reasoning or down for speed. No closing revert is needed — the backend clears agent-driven overrides automatically when the run ends, so the next user turn starts on the default model at default effort; reset_to_default() is optional mid-run only. Also includes a planning-mode protocol: draft on standard, assess complexity, optionally upgrade to premium for the final plan, and deliver a model recommendation. Load when the user asks to change models or effort, when settling in for image-heavy work, when entering plan mode, or when a task is light/heavy enough to warrant tuning the model or its thinking depth.

levels.conservative: MODEL-SWITCHING POSTURE — Conservative: stay on your default model at its default effort. Only switch model, or raise reasoning effort, when the user explicitly asks or when you are genuinely stuck and a stronger model / deeper thinking is the clear remedy. Do not proactively upgrade or raise effort.
levels.eager: MODEL-SWITCHING POSTURE — Eager: actively right-size your model AND its reasoning effort to the work. Before a task, rate how much thinking it needs: for genuinely hard reasoning or planning, raise the effort with set_effort (or upgrade to the premium model), and for light/mechanical work drop the effort down for speed; switch onto the vision model whenever a task involves looking at images. No closing revert is needed — the backend returns the chat to the default model and effort automatically when the run ends; use reset_to_default() mid-run only if you want to drop back before the run finishes. Don't grind on the cheap default — or burn high effort on trivia — when a better fit is available. (Still ask before a change that costs more.)

guidance.no_premium_model: No premium model is configured, so there's nothing stronger to upgrade onto. Tell the user plainly that an admin can assign the Premium role to a capable model in App Config → Models. Do NOT pretend you switched.

settings.label: Model switching
settings.hint: How readily this agent changes its own model and reasoning effort. Conservative = stay on the default at default effort unless asked or stuck; Balanced = upgrade or raise effort only for genuinely hard steps; Eager = proactively right-size the model and the thinking depth per task (raise effort/upgrade for hard reasoning, lower it for speed, switch to the vision model for image work). Cleanup to the default model and effort is automatic at run end — no closing revert step. This rides along as a posture note in the agent's prompt — a nudge, not a hard rule.
